The rash has persisted for 5 months without complete resolution. To help narrow this down, have you noticed any specific triggers like heat, sweating, or stress that worsen the itching?

Also, can you describe the texture of the rash—is it scaly, bumpy, or flat? And have you noticed any changes in your nails or joints?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

The chronic, pruritic nature of your bilateral upper extremity rash, combined with the absence of fever or joint pain, strongly suggests a parasitic infestation rather than an allergic reaction or infection. While scabies is more common in the web spaces of the hands and wrists, the forearms can also be involved.
